distractors.value: 6 counters (12 divided by the top number, 2)

intervention.script: Watch: 2/3 of 12 -> Step 1: 12 divided by 3 (the bottom) is 4. Step 2: 4 times 2 (the top) is 8.

labels.evidence_span: split the 12 into 3 equal groups first

learner_evidence.explanation: you split the 12 into 3 equal groups first, that's 4 each, then you take 2 of the groups so it's 8

caveats: transfer confirmed with an area-model garden bed only; a number-line/time version not yet attempted
mastery_outcome.claim: Ava can find a fraction of a set of objects

misconception.citation: Research on children's difficulty transferring fraction understanding from area models to set/group models.
misconception.cognitive_origin: When asked for a fraction of a GROUP of objects rather than a single shape, children map the wrong number in the fraction onto the partitioning step, using the numerator as the divisor instead of the denominator — a failure to transfer the part-whole model from area to a set/group model.
sprout_forbidden: stating you divide by the denominator before resolution
misconception.title: Fraction of a set means dividing by the numerator, not the denominator

skill.title: Find a fraction of a set of objects

sprout_forbidden: stating you divide by the denominator before resolution

sprout_scripts.utterance: 2/3 of 12? Easy, just divide by the top number: 12 divided by 2 is 6!
